title: Region safety harness: health-gating and staged failover automation
creator: Liam Chen
description: Goal: implement a Region Safety Harness that gates cross-region failovers using a health-gating policy and staged activation sequence for pre-warmed regional pools. This ticket captures the orchestration pieces, readiness assertions, and automation scripts to safely move traffic between regions and swap to compatible model variants when capacity or model errors trigger fallback. The harness should minimize failed requests, avoid cascading cold-starts, and provide deterministic rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A health-gating controller that evaluates a region endpoint against a composite readiness score (latency SLO, error-rate window, available slots, KV-cache hit estimate) before enabling it for live traffic.

Staged activation sequence that transitions a region from COLD -> WARM -> LIVE with idempotent steps: allocate pool, warm kv/prefix cache, perform smoke-test prompts, enable routing weight increments.

Automatic model-variant fallback: when primary model variant is unavailable or degraded, routing automatically fails over to a pre-configured compatible variant in the same or another region with minimal token loss and traceability (request tags).
Graceful drain and rollback: ability to quiesce region, drain in-flight requests, and roll back routing weights within configured timeouts if smoke tests fail at any stage.
End-to-end integration tests that simulate region outage, partial capacity, and model-serving errors and assert no user-facing 5xx spikes beyond the agreed incident window.
technical_notes: Readiness score computed as weighted sum: 50% 99th latency delta vs baseline, 30% recent error ratio (1m and 5m windows), 20% capacity headroom. Thresholds configurable per-customer tier.
KV/prefix cache warming strategy: replay representative prefix set from S3 snapshot into target pool and validate KV hit rate with synthetic traces before promotion.
Routing control plane will use staged weight shifts (10% increments every 15s) with per-route circuit breaker checks to abort or revert if error ratio climbs above threshold.

Model-variant compatibility matrix stored in catalog service; compatibility includes tokenizer match, max-seq compatibility, and quantization profile. Fallback selection prefers same-arch smaller-quantized variant in same region before cross-region choices.
State machine implemented as Kubernetes operator in control-plane namespace; operator persists orchestration state and emits events for Console and PagerDuty.
Observability: instrumentation added to trace each transition step; metrics: readiness_score, warm_duration_seconds, promotion_failures_total, fallback_activations_total.
Security: agent used for cache warming runs with customer-scoped kms keys; warming inputs are scrubbed and test prompts never persist to customer logs.
Trade-offs: aggressive warming reduces cold-start latency but increases GPU time and cost. We default to warming only for routes with >500 qps historical or enterprise customers unless overridden.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): deploy operator and gating logic to staging with synthetic region simulators; run chaos tests (terminate region instances, network blackhole) and validate state machine behavior.
Phase 2 (canary): enable safety harness for a small subset of customer routes (internal and low-risk tenants). Observe metrics for 48h and run scripted failover drills.
Phase 3 (gradual enable): expand to 25% of production routes with conservative thresholds, monitor cost impact and false-positive gating events.
Phase 4 (GA): enable default for Dedicated and Private customers; provide opt-in for Hosted routes with auto-threshold tuning.
Rollback: feature flag disables automatic promotions and falls back to previous weight controller; operator emits post-mortem-ready logs for any revert.
qa_checks: Unit tests for readiness score computation with boundary cases.
Integration tests that validate idempotency of staged activation steps.
Load tests to ensure warming sequence does not destabilize busy regional pools.
Chaos scenarios: mid-warm failure, KV cache corruption simulation, model variant mismatches.
Security review of cache-warming agent and KMS usage (separate ticket if required).
